Show HN: Bwat turns what's said in Zoom meetings into todos for your agents
items.summary: Hi All, I'm Kanton, one of the makers of bwat. Our team at Qoral built bwat because we wanted an easy way to take what we were talking about in meetings and get that work to our agent sessions with full context and quickly start them working. So we created a Zoom app that is a board that generates cards based off the transcripts of the meeting. Transcription happens with Deepgram and has user attribution, voice isolation, and all the benefits of a native Zoom app. The cards are todos (the work), unanswered questions, open risks, and decisions that have been made. They change over the course of the meeting, getting closed or updated based off the conversation. JEV helps to make these dynamic changes. Users can assign work to themselves by just saying so, instantaneously. We worked on the setup and install process to try and make it as straight forward as possible. Setting up a Zoom app isn't able to be fully automated. The source code is available. Bring your own keys. We'd most like to hear if people find this intuitive and can see the value in the meetings. It's certainly helped us with alignment and quick actions in our workflow. Thanks!

items.title: Show HN: Open-source firmware for 2011 Bowers and Wilkins Zeppelin Air
items.summary: Just wanted to share something I've built. It's fully reverse engineered, running on an old 2.4 Linux kernel I found on Nokia HD-1, but with a modern all-Rust userspace. Support Airplay 2 and Snapcast. The Airplay 2 implementation synchronizes with real Apple devices down to 1ms in the multi-room configuration. Spotify support is present, but it doesn't work for me because of librespot key issues. It utilizes the MIPS co-processor cores I have found on it for audio decoding and crypto. There's no FPU on the ARM nor the MIPS, so all the codecs are reimplemented in fixed-point math and made to fit the very small shared SRAM buffers. The DSP board firmware is also completely replaced. It fixes all the complaints I had about the original device: no source auto-switching, USB audio would de-enumerate when the speaker went to sleep, volume keys were sending HID events instead of using the proper UAC status interrupt endpoint, etc. I tried getting 24b USB audio to work, but unfortunately the endpoint buffers on this old AVR32 are too small. The the network audio supports full 44.1/48/24b though. The Wi-Fi chip is very old, there's no upgrading that, so realtime ALAC on Airplay or PCM/FLAC on Snapcast can be spotty if the connection isn't perfect, but Ethernet works too. The iPod dock doesn't work, mainly because I can't find my old iPod anywhere to develop against. Send PRs if you have one! Also partly for vanity and partly for UX I updated the LED colors and FX.

items.title: Show HN: Langfuse AI Gateway, open source rust gateway to trace every LLM call
items.summary: Hi HN, this is Max, Marc and Clemens, co-founders of Langfuse, the open source tool for agent & observability & evals ( https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse ). It’s been a minute since our last Show HN in August 2023 ( https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=37310070 ) - we’ve been busy building out and serving our tracing & eval pieces over the past years and have been very lucky to build a successful company and open source project around it. Today, we are happy to show the beta of Langfuse AI Gateway: https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/tree/main/ai-gateway . You may ask, why an AI Gateway as our second product: it’s been one our community’s strongest asks + integration pattern that we’ve seen. We want to offer a scalable, reliable and secure way to solve for the gateway use case in the same way that we’ve done with tracing/evals over the past years. And we’ve recently grown our team with some excellent folks - expect to see more bigger bets from us. Our observability SDKs currently see the code you instrument. Much of a company's model traffic runs through code that is not or cannot be easily instrumented: coding agents like Pi, Claude Code and Codex, internal tools, scripts etc. Third party gateways are already popular ways to emit traces to Langfuse and we’re happy to now ship one natively. You change your base URL and your API key. Langfuse AI Gateway forwards the native request with a provider key that does not need to be distributed across the team. Right now, it doesn't translate between APIs, responses are relayed unchanged. This was a conscious decision to ensure stability for gateway users, as translation between e.g. OpenAI responses and Anthropic messages are imperfect and might lead to subtle failures in your agents. If you pass a traceparent header, the call lands inside your existing Langfuse traces. You can try by docker composing langfuse up and then on to http://localhost:3000 -- git clone https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse.git cd langfuse docker compose up -- On Cloud, each call becomes a Langfuse generation with tokens, cost, latency and time to first token. Prompts and outputs are recorded if you opt in. If you self-hosted you can also track nothing, not even metadata. Some details: - Written in Rust. Stateless, with no database; it talks only to the Langfuse platform and the providers. - 22MB Docker image. Under 3ms median overhead with tracing on, 1,000+ concurrent streams on 2 vCPUs. - MIT licensed. Self-host it with Docker Compose or Helm or use our Cloud version. - Your provider keys and contracts. We don't resell tokens. What’s next? - Budget caps per key, user, team - Custom model aliases and fallbacks - Guardrails - PII redaction - SCIM user provisioning We’ll be around & looking forward to all questions & comments
